title: Five IT SLA commitments worth checking
intro: Before relying on an IT service agreement, compare its explicit promises with your requirements. These five checks help locate questions to resolve; they do not certify a supplier or replace professional review.

sections.heading: 1. Separate response from resolution
sections.text: A 30-minute response target promises an initial response, not a fix in 30 minutes. Check incident severity, coverage hours, when the clock starts and what qualifies as a response. Fictional example: a 60-minute response commitment is outside a stated 30-minute upper bound, assuming identical definitions and scope.

sections.heading: 2. Define the uptime calculation
sections.text: Ask which service is measured, over what window, and which exclusions apply. For illustration only, 99.9% uptime over exactly 30 days permits 43.2 minutes of downtime before exclusions. A percentage alone cannot establish whether maintenance, a regional outage or your application is covered.

sections.heading: 3. Keep RTO and RPO distinct
sections.text: A recovery time objective concerns the targeted time to restore operation. A recovery point objective concerns the tolerated data-loss window. A backup schedule is not proof that either recovery objective is achievable. Request recovery-test evidence and verify the relevant workload and assumptions.

sections.heading: 4. State support coverage explicitly
sections.text: Business-hours support and 24/7 support are different commitments. Confirm time zones, holidays, severity restrictions and who can open an incident. Do not infer 24/7 coverage merely from a promise of continuous monitoring.

sections.heading: 5. Ask for operational and independent evidence
sections.text: An escalation process should describe triggers, responsibilities and next steps. A certification claim needs independent verification of scope and validity. Automated text checks can locate gaps or conflicting values; they cannot establish whether a claim is true.

approval.scope: Publish this checklist and its existing free-product link only; no spending, outreach, new product or live payments.
